_comment: Built-in code-creation/testing benchmark tasks. Each runs in a fresh, offline Ubuntu VM. 'check' is a bash script run after the agent's turn; its exit code (0 = pass) and stdout become the score. 'seed' files (if any) are placed in /home/bench/work before the agent starts. Edit or add entries freely; ids must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$.

tasks.title: FizzBuzz CLI tool
tasks.prompt: In /home/bench/work, write an executable file named 'fizzbuzz' (Python or a shell script, your choice; make it executable with chmod +x) that takes no arguments and prints the numbers 1 to 100, one per line, except: for multiples of 3 print 'Fizz', for multiples of 5 print 'Buzz', and for multiples of both print 'FizzBuzz'. When you are done, reply with a short confirmation.

tasks.title: Fix a broken function so its tests pass
tasks.prompt: There is a small Python package in /home/bench/work. Its tests (in test_stats.py) currently fail. Look at the code in stats.py, find the bug(s), and fix stats.py so that running 'pytest -q' in /home/bench/work passes all tests. Do not edit test_stats.py. Reply with a short summary of what was wrong when you are done.

tasks.title: Minimal REST API with a health endpoint
tasks.prompt: In /home/bench/work, write a small web server (app.py, using Python's standard library http.server or Flask - both are installed) that listens on 0.0.0.0:8000 and responds to GET /health with HTTP 200 and the JSON body {"status": "ok"}. Include a file named 'run.sh' (executable) that starts the server in the background (e.g. with nohup ... & ) and exits immediately so the terminal is free afterward. Reply with a short confirmation when it is running.
tasks.check:
set -e
cd /home/bench/work
test -x run.sh || { echo 'run.sh is missing or not executable'; exit 1; }
./run.sh
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
  out=$(curl -s -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:8000/health || true)
  [ -n "$out" ] && break
  sleep 1
done
echo "response: $out"
python3 - <<PY
import json
try:
    d = json.loads('''$out''')
except Exception as e:
    print('not valid JSON:', e); raise SystemExit(1)
if d.get('status') != 'ok':
    print('expected status:ok, got', d); raise SystemExit(1)
print('health endpoint OK')
PY
